messages:
OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected in control-plane deps (org-lookup + auth proxy). Auto-pager sent to #incidents and on-call. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/ctrlplane/health?panelId=7
Tess (sre): acked — I'm on it. Pulling recent deployment and gateway logs.
Marco (eng-oncall): I'm nearby. Any customer-facing errors reported yet?
Liam (support): getting inbound tickets from 3 customers reporting failed model calls, K = enterprise tier. Error examples show 502 gateway.
Priya (infra): Seeing spike across frontends hitting auth-token endpoint, 504s from auth cluster. Rolling window: 2m spike to 18% 5xx.
Tess (sre): timeline: starts ~5219876400, correlates with a config rollout to org-lookup (feature: multi-tenant caching) at 5219876000.
Marco (eng-oncall): Good catch. Suggest immediate mitigation: route traffic away from new org-lookup instance group, fallback to stable variant. Can infra apply routing rule?
Priya (infra): Doing sni proxy change now: `kubectl patch svc org-lookup -n controlplane -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"stable"}}}'` — applying. Will route new requests within ~15s.
Tess (sre): While that happens, enable 5xx alert suppression for noisy metrics to avoid pager storms: `opsctl alerts mute --alert=ctrlplane-5xx --duration=30m --reason="mitigating"`
Marco (eng-oncall): Also flip the circuit-breaker to fail-open for downstream billing calls to avoid cascading timeouts. `config: billing.timeout=300ms -> 100ms` (we'll revert).
Priya (infra): Route change applied. Observability: error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in ~40s.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: rollback detected for org-lookup service (deploy id: dpl-2026-05-02-78).
Tess (sre): Nice. Keep monitoring. Marco, can you check auth token cache pressure? Logs show `TokenCache::Evict` spikes and `OOM`-adjacent GC pauses.
Marco (eng-oncall): Looking. Auth pods show increased heap and GC churn. There's a recent JVM flag change in the auth release earlier today: `-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200`. Reverting might help.
Ken (product): Any known customers impacted? Need to prepare comms. Priority?
Liam (support): So far ~3 enterprise tickets, + ~120 user API errors per minute on the public status page. Might be broader but mostly write-heavy flows. Customers: AcmeCorp, SprintDesk, StudyAI.
Tess (sre): Classification: partial degradation of control plane auth/org-lookup affecting 10-15% of requests, severe for a small subset of enterprise customers. Start incident doc and severity: Sev2.
Marco (eng-oncall): I pushed a hotfix to auth: revert JVM flag and bump thread-pool config back to pre-release values. Rolling restart of auth pods now: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth -n controlplane`
Priya (infra): Rolling restart initiated. Watchers: /api/health/auth now stable responses from new pods.
OpsBot: Pager duty note: oncall escalation - primary -> secondary handoff in 10m.
Tess (sre): I'll stay primary for mitigation; Marco please shadow and take next shift when OpsBot hands off. Ken, draft an interim status: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx for some API calls; a partial rollback is in progress. No customer data loss reported."
Ken (product): On it. Sending to comms channel and support template.
Marco (eng-oncall): After restart, auth latency back to normal and 5xx baseline -> ~1.2%. Org-lookup fallbacks still at low error.
Liam (support): Closing tickets: leaving standard workaround note (retry, backoff). Sent proactive messages to AcmeCorp and StudyAI.
Tess (sre): Actions so far: 1) routed traffic off new org-lookup instances 2) rolled back org-lookup deploy 3) reverted auth JVM change + restarted 4) temporary billing CB relaxation.
Priya (infra): Telemetry indicates stabilization across regions us-west/us-east/eu-west. No sign of DB saturation.
Marco (eng-oncall): Root cause hypothesis: combined config rollouts (org-lookup caching + auth JVM tuning) interacted under spike workload — cache pressure + GC churn -> timeouts -> gateway 5xx.
Tess (sre): Next steps: postmortem owner? Recommend eng-runtime + infra co-author, include revert plan and improved rollout safety (circuit-breaker defaults, gradual canary with load tests).
Ken (product): Assigning PM follow-up. I'll collect impacted customer list and coordinate comms.
OpsBot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors remain below threshold for 30m, we'll resolve.
Tess (sre): Agreed. Handoff: Marco you'll be secondary; Priya please stay until 5219877000 to ensure no regression.
Marco (eng-oncall): Acknowledged. I'll take over if OpsBot escalates.
Priya (infra): Staying on watch.
Liam (support): I'll keep support triage open for 1h, will escalate any new enterprise reports.
Tess (sre): Closing notes for thread: mitigation successful, partial rollback and JVM revert restored baseline. Still tracking RCA and postmortem. Thanks team. :clap:
